bull.b: Very large, growing free cash flow that converts near 95% of net income provides durable internal funding for R&D, capex, repurchases and strategic partnerships. Strong FCF supports long‑run reinvestment and capital returns even if margins normalize, enhancing financial optionality.

Extremely low leverage and substantial equity growth give the company durable financial flexibility to fund supply expansion, strategic hires, and large financing programs without stressing liquidity. The conservative base reduces refinancing risk and preserves runway during cyclical demand shifts.

Market‑leading GPU architectures, benchmark dominance and deep software ecosystem (CUDA/platforms) create a durable competitive moat. Strong hyperscaler and frontier model adoption locks in scale advantages, driving sustained data‑center demand, pricing power and ecosystem stickiness over multiple quarters.

bear.b: Heavy prepaid supply commitments and constrained advanced packaging/foundry capacity create execution risk that can persist for quarters. Supply bottlenecks can force allocation, delay customer builds, and lock capital in inventory or prepaids, limiting responsiveness to demand shifts.

Excluding China compute from guidance highlights a material geopolitical/regulatory tail risk to revenue visibility in a large market. Prolonged export or licensing uncertainty can reduce addressable demand, complicate capacity planning and weaken long‑term growth assumptions.

Rapid OpEx acceleration (compensation, infra, R&D) reduces operating leverage and raises the revenue growth needed to sustain margins. If top‑line growth moderates, higher fixed costs could compress operating margins and make profitability more cyclical over the next several quarters.
